editorial.headline: Private Film Distribution: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This paid private distribution activity spans cinema, television, exhibitors and distribution rights—nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Private film, video and television-programme distribution is, at its core, the paid circulation of moving-image work. The activity covers distributing films, videos and comparable audiovisual productions to motion-picture cinemas or big-screen theatres, television networks and stations, and exhibitors, where the work is privately managed on a fee basis. It also expressly includes distribution of sports-media content in film, video and television programmes. The scope therefore reaches the channels named in the record: cinema, television and exhibition.

The definition also reaches the acquisition of distribution rights to moving pictures, including films, videos, audiovisual works and similar productions, when privately managed. That places both the distribution of content and the acquisition of the rights to distribute it within the activity’s stated terrain. The code is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar enterprises, placing it across the full range of scales identified in the record. The registrant is a private operator engaged in that paid distribution activity or in obtaining those distribution rights.

At the national level, the foreign-investment position is clear. The activity is TERBUKA—open—and the maximum foreign ownership is 100%. A foreign investor therefore encounters a nationally open classification with full foreign ownership permitted. The stated basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national position applies to the distribution activity described here, including its cinema, television, exhibitor and sports-media distribution elements, as well as the stated acquisition of distribution rights.

Bali changes the outcome for PMA registration. Its Bali status is Blocked (risk class): blocked by risk class. At the Besar scale, every scope carries an OSS risk of Rendah or Menengah-Rendah. Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for activities with Low and Medium-Low risk. Since this activity is caught by that rule, a foreigner cannot register it in Bali today. The block is not a reduction of the national 100% ceiling; it is a Bali registration prohibition under the moratorium introduced in May 2026.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open at 100%, this activity is nevertheless unavailable for PMA registration in Bali under the island-wide moratorium.
